meta.titre: The Informal Sector in Cameroon: features, benefits to the economy and drawbacks
meta.sous_theme: Meaning, features, advantages and problems of the informal sector

sections.contenu_markdown: At Mokolo market in Yaounde and at roadside stalls in Douala, many people earn a living without any registered shop or payroll. Many of these small traders are not registered with the tax office. This is the informal sector, and the GCE paper asks what it is, what it contributes and what harm it causes. Learning to separate its benefits from its drawbacks wins easy marks in the multiple-choice section.

items: Economic activities produce goods and services that people buy to meet their needs.
Governments collect taxes from businesses and people to pay for public services.
Unemployment means that people who are able and willing to work cannot find a paid job.

sections.titre: What the informal sector is and what it does for the economy
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Definition
The **informal sector** is made up of small economic activities that are not officially registered, are largely outside government regulation, and usually do not pay taxes or keep formal accounts. In Cameroon it includes street sellers roadside tailors, mechanics working in open yards, small food sellers, motorbike taxi riders and small workshops. The **formal sector** is the opposite: registered firms, written contracts, tax payment and regular records.

### Features
| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| Small capital | A person can start with savings or family loans |
| Family or small labour | Workers are often relatives or apprentices |
| No registration | The business is not registered, so it usually escapes taxes |
| Local materials and simple tools | Low technology; goods are made and repaired locally |
| Flexible hours | Opening times and prices change with customers |

### Advantages to the economy
- It provides jobs and incomes for many people, including young people and school leavers, so it reduces unemployment and poverty.
- It sells cheap goods and services that low-income families can afford.
- It trains people through apprenticeship and allows them to start a business with little money.
- It uses local raw materials and recycles, and it spreads goods to places the formal shops do not serve.

### Problems
- Government loses tax revenue, which could pay for roads, schools and hospitals.
- Workers have low and uncertain pay, no contract and little social protection.
- Working conditions can be unsafe, and street trading can cause traffic jams, litter and pollution.
- Quality and standards are hard to control, and the sector is difficult to measure for planning.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a multiple-choice question asks which item is not an advantage
variantes.contenu_markdown: Ask who benefits. Jobs, cheap goods and low start-up costs benefit people and the economy. Not paying tax or lacking worker protection hurts government revenue or workers, so it is a problem. Check whether the question asks for a feature (what the sector is like) or an advantage (what good it does): one item can be a feature and a problem at once.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the command word is explain, discuss or account for the importance of the sector
variantes.contenu_markdown: Choose two or three points, develop each in a full sentence with a reason and a Cameroonian example, then add one balancing problem if the question says discuss. A list of single words earns few marks.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain two ways in which the informal sector helps the Cameroonian economy and describe one problem that it creates.

etapes.action: Read the command word and the numbers.
etapes.justification: Explain means give a reason for each point; the question asks for two benefits and one problem, so the answer needs three developed points.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Plan: benefit 1 (jobs), benefit 2 (affordable goods), problem (lost tax).

etapes.action: Develop benefit 1 with a reason and an example.
etapes.justification: A statement alone scores little; the reason and the example earn the second mark.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Jobs: roadside tailors and moto-taxi riders earn an income without a formal employer, so unemployment is reduced.

etapes.justification: The link to people's welfare must be stated.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Affordable goods: street sellers offer small quantities at low prices, which families with small incomes can buy.

etapes.justification: A problem needs its consequence for the economy.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Lost tax: most informal businesses are not registered, so the government collects little revenue to build schools and roads.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: The informal sector provides jobs, because roadside tailors, mechanics and moto-taxi riders earn an income without a formal employer, so unemployment is reduced. It also supplies goods at prices that low-income families can afford, since street sellers offer small quantities cheaply. However, most informal businesses are not registered and do not pay tax, so government revenue is low and less money is available for schools and roads.

items.erreur_markdown: "The informal sector is illegal activity such as smuggling and theft."
items.pourquoi_faux: The informal sector is mostly lawful work done in small unregistered businesses. Crime is a separate matter.
items.correction_markdown: The informal sector means small, unregistered but mostly legal business activities such as street selling and roadside repairs.

items.erreur_markdown: "Paying no tax is an advantage of the informal sector to the economy."
items.pourquoi_faux: Avoiding tax benefits the owner but reduces government revenue, so it harms public services.
items.correction_markdown: Failure to pay tax is a feature and a problem. Advantages to the economy are jobs, cheap goods and low start-up costs.

items.erreur_markdown: "Only poor and uneducated people work in the informal sector."
items.pourquoi_faux: Many educated people also work in it because formal jobs are scarce.
items.correction_markdown: People of different education levels work in the sector; it is a way to earn an income when formal jobs are few.

items.erreur_markdown: "A market stall that employs relatives is part of the formal sector because it has workers."
items.pourquoi_faux: Having workers does not make a business formal. Formal means registered, taxed and keeping records, with contracts.
items.correction_markdown: A stall employing relatives without a registration or contracts is informal.

items.enonce_markdown: Classify each activity as formal or informal: (a) a bank branch with registered staff, (b) a roadside tailor, (c) a registered supermarket, (d) a woman selling tomatoes at a street corner.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Formal.** (b) **Informal.** (c) **Formal.** (d) **Informal.** Reason: formal businesses are registered, pay taxes and use contracts; the informal ones are small, unregistered and unrecorded.

items.enonce_markdown: A town has 12,000 workers; 8,400 of them work in the informal sector. (a) What percentage of workers is informal? (b) A seamstress in this town earns FCFA 4,500 per day and works 26 days in a month. What is her monthly income?

A council wants to register 800 market traders and charge each one a flat tax of FCFA 12,000 per year. (a) How much would it collect if all traders paid? (b) How much would it collect if only 65% paid? (c) How much revenue is lost? (d) Suggest two ways to encourage traders to register, and give one reason why many traders resist.
items.solution_markdown: (a) 800 × 12,000 = **FCFA 9,600,000**. (b) 65% of 800 traders = 520 traders; 520 × 12,000 = **FCFA 6,240,000**. (c) Loss = 9,600,000 − 6,240,000 = **FCFA 3,360,000**. (d) Ways: keep the tax low and simple; give registered traders benefits such as secure market stalls, cheap loans or training. Reasons for resistance (one is enough): fear that the tax will reduce their small profit, or a belief that they get no services in return.

items_markdown: The informal sector is made of small, mostly unregistered and untaxed economic activities such as street selling, roadside repairs and moto-taxis.
Advantages: jobs, income, cheap goods, easy start with little capital, apprenticeship and use of local materials.
Problems: loss of tax revenue, low pay without protection, unsafe or crowded working places and difficulty in planning.
In a multiple-choice question decide who benefits: avoiding tax does not benefit the economy.
Explain questions need a point, a reason and a Cameroonian example for each answer.
